title: Great is your faith (Matthew 15:21–39)
hook: left on read, she asks again, shorter, and finds room in his own words
tomorrow: how does one sour comment take over a whole group?

segments.voice: Yesterday, hands at a table and a list that starts with thoughts. From the heart. Today, a woman who will not stop asking.

Left on read. The three dots appear, then vanish. So you ask again, shorter this time. A woman in Matthew knows that silence. She's from Canaan, from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, outside Israel, and her daughter is suffering. She follows Jesus and his friends down the road, calling out: "Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou son of David." Then a line that stops the scene cold: "But he answered her not a word." The disciples want her gone. She doesn't go.
screen: `LEFT ON READ.` → `HAVE MERCY ON ME.` → `NOT A WORD.`

segments.voice: His first answer is about his mission: "I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel." She comes closer, kneels, and makes her request shorter: "Lord, help me." His second answer is harder still: "It is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to dogs." These are difficult words to hear. Some readers take them as a test of her; some hear Jesus' mission widening, right there in the conversation. Matthew doesn't say which. What Matthew does show is her answer. She doesn't argue with the picture. She steps inside it: "Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table." Bread, a table, crumbs. She takes his own image and finds room in it for her daughter. And this time he answers her fully: "O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt." Her daughter is made whole from that very hour. Notice who gets the praise. Not a disciple. A mother from outside, who kept asking, each time shorter and plainer. Then Matthew moves on to a hillside where a crowd is fed from seven loaves, and baskets of broken pieces are left over. Right after she asks for crumbs.
screen: `NOT A WORD, THEN NOT SENT.` · `LORD, HELP ME.` · `YET THE DOGS EAT OF THE CRUMBS.` · `O WOMAN, GREAT IS THY FAITH.`

segments.voice: Write by hand the name of someone you keep asking for, for healing, for a job, for a way back. Her words, Lord, help me, are short enough to write beside the name. Look at the two together while you breathe.
Great is your faith. What Jesus says to a Canaanite mother who wouldn't stop asking, and who found room for her daughter in his own words.
Your line: great is your faith, said to someone who simply kept asking. Rest easy.

howItsDone: Some Christians keep a prayer list of people they ask for again and again, and some churches read the Canaanite woman's story as a picture of persistent prayer.

chat.says: asked Pop 3 times to come hear us sing Sunday. he keeps saying maybe. do i stop asking?
options: Keep asking, gently and shorter each time. The woman in Matthew 15 kept finding room.
Stop. If he wanted to come, he'd have said yes the very first time that you asked.
Hand it off to the pastor to call him; it's really not your place to keep asking.
chat.meaning: Met with silence, the Canaanite mother asked again, shorter each time, and Jesus said: O woman, great is thy faith.

Canaan.meaning: an old name for the land and its earlier peoples

Tyre and Sidon.meaning: coastal cities outside Israel, named in Matthew 15:21

son of David.meaning: a title for the promised king from David's line

notes: The 'dogs' saying is presented with 'some readers take them as a test of her; some hear Jesus' mission widening'. Confirm both readings are fairly put and that neither is ranked.
'Outside Israel' for the coasts of Tyre and Sidon is a summary; confirm.

The link between the crumbs and the leftover baskets (15:37) is presented as Matthew's order of events, not as a claim about his intent. The four thousand and the seven baskets are not counted in the voice.
The practice uses her prayer 'Lord, help me' (15:25), a real text, offered beside a name; no 'if you pray' formula today.
Trapdoor floor 3 links the praise of her faith to the centurion (8:10, 'I have not found so great faith'). Confirm.
Grace storyline day 12: Pop has not come back to Sunday singing since Mr. Hollis died; Grace has asked three times and he keeps saying maybe. The wrong options are 'stop' and 'hand it off'.
